paths.title: Chong Xie → Zhengtuo Zhao
paths.summary: Follow Zhao's PhD training in Xie's group, then open his wider research network. His doctorate was awarded by UT Austin; his later postdoctoral work included Rice.

relationships.description: Xie's alumni roster lists Zhengtuo Zhao as a PhD student in the group, with a 2015–2020 lab interval.
relationships.limit: The lab interval is not the doctorate's duration. The roster supports lab training; it does not independently establish sole formal dissertation supervision.

relationships.description: Zhao's UCAS biography dates his UT Austin biomedical engineering doctorate to September 2015–August 2019, followed by a UT Austin/Rice postdoc interval in 2019–2020.

paths.title: One paper, different author roles
paths.summary: See how Zhengtuo Zhao and Chong Xie contributed to the same 2017 nanoelectronic-thread study. The paper makes their authorship roles explicit.

relationships.description: The original paper names Zhao, Lan Luan and Xiaoling Wei as equal contributors.

source.title: 2017 NET paper — original article at UT Austin

relationships.limit: These are selected contributors from a larger author team. Authorship alone does not establish patent ownership or a company license.

relationships.description: The same article identifies Xie as its corresponding author, with a UT Austin affiliation.

source.title: 2017 NET paper — author and affiliation information

paths.title: Zhengtuo Zhao + Xue Li → StairMed
paths.summary: Two researchers connect to the same company through disclosed founder roles. Follow each person to their training, papers and technology links.

relationships.description: The 2026 human uFINE paper's competing-interest disclosure identifies Zhengtuo Zhao as a StairMed founder.
relationships.limit: A founder relationship does not establish a license from the earlier NET research or equate the study device with a marketed implant.

relationships.description: The same disclosure identifies Xue Li as a StairMed founder alongside Zhao.

paths.title: Benjamin Rapoport → two companies
paths.summary: A shared founder connects Neuralink and Precision Neuroscience. Open the two documented roles to understand the connection.

relationships.description: Precision's official leadership biography identifies Rapoport as a Neuralink co-founder before Precision.
relationships.limit: This is a historical founding role, not a statement of current employment.

relationships.description: Precision identifies Rapoport as its co-founder and Chief Science Officer.
relationships.limit: A shared founder does not establish a corporate spinout, subsidiary relationship or technology license between the companies.

paths.title: Thomas Oxley + Nicholas Opie → Synchron
paths.summary: Follow two co-founders into the endovascular interface story. Melbourne's account connects their company to university and clinical research.

relationships.description: The University of Melbourne credits Oxley and Opie with founding Synchron in 2012.

source.title: University of Melbourne — Synchron commercialization story

relationships.description: The same university account identifies Opie as a co-founder alongside Oxley.

source.title: University of Melbourne — Synchron commercialization story

relationships.limit: These sources document co-founders and shared research, not a mentor–trainee relationship between the two people.

paths.title: Jacob Robinson → Rice lab → Motif
paths.summary: A founder role and an explicitly documented lab spinout connect Robinson's university research to Motif. Explore the people and work behind its neuromodulation devices.

relationships.description: Rice identifies Robinson as a Motif founder and CEO in its January 2025 research announcement.

source.title: Rice — brain research awards and Motif's research roots

relationships.description: Rice explicitly describes Motif as a startup that spun out of Robinson's Rice laboratory.

source.title: Rice — brain research awards and Motif's research roots

relationships.limit: This account establishes a lab spinout; it does not specify the terms of a technology license.
